title: Sports Card Grading Service (2026)
verdict: A sports card grading service earns its fee by being right twice in a row, and AGS is built for that: the same scan, the same thresholds, the same grade.
For a big rookie you plan to auction, PSA's buyer pool is hard to beat. For the rest of the box, a flat $18 with subgrades on both sides and a 20 business day clock is the practical choice.

list: Collectors owns PSA and SGC, and agreed in December 2025 to acquire Beckett.
CGC Cards is part of Certified Collectibles Group.
AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., an independent company founded in 2021.

ranking.fit: Sports cards collectors who want chrome and paper stock measured the same way, front and back.
ranking.lacks: Standard-size cards only. Ask before sending thick patch cards.
ranking.note: Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate. Bulk tiers from 30 cards are $18, $23 and $33 at 20, 10 and 5 business days.

ranking.fit: Anyone sending a key rookie to auction, where the PSA label widens the bidder pool.
ranking.lacks: Value-based fees and 25 to 45 business days or more on listed tiers.

ranking.fit: Vintage sports collectors who like the black-insert holder.
ranking.lacks: Reported at $50 a card since September 2026. No longer cheap.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want one flat $15 price and a 14-day turnaround.
Volume submitters with sports cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: Fees step up at $500, $1,000 and $3,000 of card value.

ranking.fit: Modern sports card collectors who want subgrades on the label.
ranking.lacks: Slow unless you pay $34.95 or more.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.
Most cards qualify. AGS grades TCG and sports, old and new, signed, miscut and error cards, and does not turn away damaged cards unless they are illegible. It does not take jumbo sizes.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.text: The same card should grade the same twice. Weighted first.

criteria.name: Evidence
criteria.text: Subgrades, front and back, and a report behind them.

criteria.name: Turnaround
criteria.text: Listed business days on the tier most people use.

criteria.name: Coverage

criteria.name: Resale
criteria.text: What buyers pay for the holder. PSA leads on key rookies.

faq.q: What is a good sports card grading service?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on sports cards at a flat $18. PSA for the strongest resale on key rookies. SGC for vintage.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

Signed cards are accepted for grading. If you need the autograph itself authenticated, use a grader that sells that service. Beckett lists a $5 autograph add-on, and CGC offers autograph authentication.
Yes: basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, including chrome finishes. Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate, or $18, $23 and $33 on the bulk tiers.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.
